comparisons.peer_summary: Markets net income was $4.9 billion, an increase of 27%, driven by higher revenues and partially offset by higher cost of credit.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C discuss credit performance drivers within their commercial and consumer portfolios. BAC focuses on industry concentration growth in Finance companies, citing a $12.7 billion increase in committed exposure driven by Consumer finance and Thrifts. In contrast, C discusses the 'Markets' segment net income, noting it increased 27% driven by higher revenues but partially offset by higher cost of credit. While both reference cost of credit, BAC's disclosure is specific to industry exposure growth, whereas C's is a segment-level P&L item where cost of credit is a negative offset to revenue gains rather than a primary driver of exposure growth.

sentences.text: Finance companies, our second largest industry concentration with committed exposure of $101.8 billion, increased $12.7 billion, or 14 percent, during 2024.
The increase in committed exposure was primarily driven by increases in Consumer finance, Thrifts and mortgage finance and Diversified financials.
Markets net income of $4.9 billion increased 27%, driven by higher revenues, partially offset by higher cost of credit.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer & Retail exposure was $129.8 billion as of December 31, 2024, with criticized exposure decreasing by $1.4 billion from $8.3 billion to $6.9 billion, driven by net portfolio activity and upgrades largely offset by downgrades.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose specific industry or sector exposures and the changes in their credit quality metrics (committed exposure vs. criticized exposure) for 2024. BAC reports Finance companies as its second largest concentration with $101.8 billion in committed exposure, showing a 14% increase. JPM reports Consumer & Retail exposure at $129.8 billion, but notes that its criticized exposure (a proxy for credit deterioration) decreased by $1.4 billion. BAC highlights growth in volume for Finance companies, while JPM highlights an improvement in credit quality (lower criticized assets) for Consumer & Retail despite stable growth in total exposure.
